solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Superficial manner to plug leak

indicators.note: a plug sits inside a hole, so 'manner' goes inside 'leak'

blocks.note: to seep is to leak slowly
kind = manner, sort, as in 'of that kind'

explanation.surface: Someone with a slapdash way of stopping a leak, all show and no real repair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Plug' and 'leak' paint a plumbing job, but 'Superficial' alone is the definition; the manner word goes in just after the first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Something only surface-level, lacking any depth beneath, is described with this idiom about beauty going no further than the outer layer.

clue.text: Characters coming back from mill on Kenyan hillock

indicators.note: the letters of the answer are characters printed in the phrase that follows
the characters run from right to left, returning the way they came

blocks.note: the run spans the end of 'mill', all of 'on' and the start of 'Kenyan'

explanation.surface: Something seen returning from a mill on a small African hill.
explanation.walkthrough: Read 'milL ON Kenyan' backwards to get the answer; 'from' is the setter pointing at where the letters are.
explanation.definitionFit: A small rounded hill or mound is a synonym for a hillock; both are words for a modest rise in the ground.

clue.text: Essence is lousy and full of bits

blocks.note: lousy in its literal sense: infested with lice, full of nits
gritty = full of small hard bits

explanation.surface: A scornful review of a perfume or extract: rubbish, and full of sediment.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lousy' reads as 'bad', but here it is literal: crawling with lice, whose eggs are nits.
explanation.definitionFit: The basic, fundamental core of a matter is called the nitty-gritty in informal speech, just as its essence is its heart.

clue.text: Coterie moving around new building

indicators.note: letters moving around one another end up in a new order

blocks.note: N is the standard abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A clique relocating to a newly built block.
explanation.walkthrough: The seven letters of 'Coterie' plus N for 'new' are rearranged together.
explanation.definitionFit: A structure that has been put up, such as a house or tower, is a formal word for any constructed edifice.

clue.text: Article in truck men recover after adversity

indicators.note: 'Article' is placed in, between 'truck' and 'men'

blocks.note: a pickup is a small open-backed truck

explanation.surface: A newspaper article about lorry drivers getting back on their feet after hard times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Men' looks like people, but in games men are the playing pieces, as in chess or draughts.
explanation.definitionFit: To restore normal life once something has gone badly wrong is the meaning of this idiom about gathering broken fragments.

clue.text: About to struggle with opening shed for livestock

indicators.note: to shed is to cast off, so the word for 'struggle' casts off its opening letter

explanation.surface: A farmer about to wrestle open a shed door to get at the animals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like a farm building, which fits livestock, but it is the verb: to lose. C for circa is a common abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: Cows, bulls and oxen kept on farms are the classic example of animals raised for meat or milk.

clue.text: Short watercourse starts to deviate across land in North America

indicators.note: cut short, the watercourse word loses its last letter
the starts of the following two words are their first letters

blocks.note: CANAL with its tail cut off
first letters of these two words

explanation.surface: A brief stream meanders away across the continent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Across' pulls double duty: its first letter is used, and it reads as the joining word in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The large country occupying the northern part of that continent is one example of a nation there.

clue.text: Cardinal is extremely audible

indicators.note: what is audible is heard, so we want a word that is heard like 'extremely'

explanation.surface: A churchman in red who can be heard very clearly.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cardinal' suggests a churchman or a red bird; here it is a cardinal number, as against an ordinal like second.
explanation.definitionFit: Counting numbers such as one, two and three are called cardinal numbers, so any of them fits.

clue.text: Sticky stuff filling molten whisked dessert

indicators.note: a filling goes inside, so 'sticky stuff' is put inside the rearranged letters
whisking beats ingredients into a new mixture, so 'molten' is jumbled

explanation.surface: A pudding recipe: pour in a gooey filling and whisk the melted mixture.
explanation.walkthrough: The kitchen words 'filling', 'molten' and 'whisked' all read as cookery; only 'whisked' is really an instruction to rearrange.
explanation.definitionFit: A pastry case with a sharp citrus curd filling is a classic example of a sweet course served after dinner.

clue.text: Leisurely walk up to lost alien oddly overlooked

indicators.note: the odd-placed letters are ignored, so only the even ones count

blocks.note: the 2nd, 4th, 6th letters and so on of this run

explanation.surface: A stroll up to a stray extraterrestrial that everyone has strangely ignored.
explanation.walkthrough: The selection runs across four words, including 'up to', which reads as part of the stroll. A pootle is chiefly British, informal for an unhurried amble or drive.
explanation.definitionFit: An unhurried amble with no particular purpose is what this informal British term describes, whether on foot or by car.

clue.text: Agrees to fiddle official documents

blocks.note: to con is to swindle or fiddle
forms are official documents to fill in

explanation.surface: Someone consents to falsify the paperwork.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fiddle' as in fiddling the books, not playing the violin.
explanation.definitionFit: To comply with or match rules or expectations is a close synonym of being in accord with them.

clue.text: Parking place causing drama

blocks.note: to lay is to put or place

explanation.surface: A dispute over a parking space turning into a scene.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Drama' suggests a fuss, but it is the theatre piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A stage work performed by actors is the basic synonym for a theatrical piece.

clue.text: Below breaking object making loud noise

indicators.note: 'below' breaks into 'object', splitting it in two

explanation.surface: Something falling from above and hitting the ground with a crash.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Breaking' suggests smashing, but here it means breaking into: the object word is split after its second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Rumbling or booming like a storm overhead is how this participle describes something very noisy.

clue.text: Element of driver anger over stalling cars

indicators.note: the answer is one element, a part, of the longer run of words

blocks.note: runs from the last letter of 'driver' to the first of 'stalling'

explanation.surface: Road rage: part of a driver's fury is about stalled vehicles.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole thing reads as a driving complaint, which neatly hides a pair of car models in plain view.
explanation.definitionFit: These luxury off-road vehicles made by Land Rover are a well-known example of motor vehicles.

clue.text: Hotel chain rising in market

indicators.note: 'rising' is placed in the word for 'market'

blocks.note: a rising is an uprising, a riot

explanation.surface: A hotel group's shares going up on the stock market.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rising' looks like a verb about share prices, but it is the noun, as in the Easter Rising.
explanation.definitionFit: This American hospitality company runs a large international group of branded lodging properties.

clue.text: A very quiet London district is pleasant

blocks.note: pp = pianissimo, the musical marking for very quiet
Ealing is a district in west London

explanation.surface: An estate agent's line: this hushed suburb of London is a nice place to live.
explanation.walkthrough: Ealing is a borough in west London, famous for its film studios.
explanation.definitionFit: Attractive or agreeable, something that draws people to it, is a near synonym for nice or pleasing.

clue.text: Cycling composer is approaching

indicators.note: going round in a cycle, letters from the front move to the back

blocks.note: Thomas Arne, English composer of Rule, Britannia!

explanation.surface: A musician on a bike is getting close.
explanation.walkthrough: ARNE, a crossword favourite, has its first two letters moved to the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Coming close in space or time is what both words describe, as in 'the day is near'.

clue.text: One smells fruit ultimately in small container of fluid

indicators.note: ultimately means in the end, so only the last letter of 'fruit'
that letter goes in the word built from 'small' and 'container of fluid'

blocks.note: S = small, as on clothing labels
an inkpot holds ink, a fluid

explanation.surface: Someone sniffing fruit that has gone off in a small jar of liquid.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Smells' reads as sniffs, but the definition means someone who gives off a smell.
explanation.definitionFit: A person or thing that reeks is informally called by this insulting name, literally a pot that stinks.

clue.text: Notice spinning toys revolving

indicators.note: turning round, the toy word is read back to front

explanation.surface: Look at the whirling toys going round and round.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spinning' looks like the indicator, but it describes the toys; 'revolving' does the work.
explanation.definitionFit: To see or catch sight of something is a verb synonym, as in spotting a friend in a crowd.

clue.text: Earnest request to dine in lobby

indicators.note: 'dine' is placed in the word for 'lobby'

blocks.note: an entry is an entrance hall or lobby

explanation.surface: A heartfelt plea to be allowed to have dinner in the hotel foyer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lobby' can suggest petitioning politicians, which fits a request, but here it is the hallway.
explanation.definitionFit: A sincere, pleading appeal to someone is a formal word for a plea or supplication.

clue.text: Frustrated fat FBI agent eats

indicators.note: what eats something takes it inside, so the agent holds 'fat'

blocks.note: a fed is a US federal agent

explanation.surface: An overweight federal agent comfort-eating after a thwarted case.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads with 'Frustrated' describing the agent, but it is the definition standing alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Thwarted or prevented from succeeding is a past-participle synonym, as in a villain's plans being blocked.

clue.text: Boy in banal novel is from ancient city

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters before it take a new form

explanation.surface: A boy character in a dull book comes from some ancient place.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' looks like a joining word, but its letters are part of the fodder. 'Novel' suggests a book; it is the indicator.
explanation.definitionFit: Babylon, in Mesopotamia, was one of the great cities of antiquity, and this adjective describes its people or things.

clue.text: Gem father gets in centre of Honolulu

indicators.note: 'father' gets inside the letters chosen from the city
only the middle letters of the city's name are used

blocks.note: the middle two of its eight letters

explanation.surface: Dad finds a precious stone in downtown Hawaii.
explanation.walkthrough: Honolulu has eight letters, so its centre is the fourth and fifth, O and L.
explanation.definitionFit: This iridescent silica stone is a classic example of a precious or semi-precious jewel.

clue.text: First-rate inspector’s case journalist made public

indicators.note: a case is the outside of something, so only the outer letters of 'inspector'

explanation.surface: A top detective's case is reported openly by a newspaper writer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Case' sounds like a detective's investigation but it means the casing: the outer letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Broadcast or expressed openly, as in airing views or a programme, is a synonym for being disclosed.

clue.text: Devilish and bold, I messed with CIA

indicators.note: the letters are tampered with and put in disorder

explanation.surface: A brazen confession: wickedly, I meddled with the American spy agency.
explanation.walkthrough: The CIA is the US Central Intelligence Agency; its three letters join the five of 'bold, I'.
explanation.definitionFit: Relating to or like Satan, fiendish, is the meaning of this adjective from the Greek for slanderer.

clue.text: Signal disapproval when boozing loses its sparkle

indicators.note: 'sparkle' names the part that 'boozing' loses

explanation.surface: Heavy drinking stops being fun, so someone jeers.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing ZING from the end of 'boozing' leaves the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeering at a performer with this sound is how a crowd shows it dislikes what it sees.

clue.text: French fellow is irrational and sinned endlessly

indicators.note: without an end, the verb for 'sinned' loses its last letter

blocks.note: pi is the best-known irrational number
ERRED, to err being to sin, cut short

explanation.surface: A Frenchman described as unreasonable and a constant wrongdoer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Irrational' reads as unreasonable, but mathematically it names a number that cannot be written as a fraction.
explanation.definitionFit: A common given name in France, the equivalent of Peter, stands as a typical man from that country.

clue.text: A lodge in disrepair is ancient

indicators.note: something in disrepair has fallen apart, its parts out of order

explanation.surface: A dilapidated hut in the woods is very old.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface and answer agree nicely: a lodge in disrepair probably is ancient.
explanation.definitionFit: Having existed for a very long time, venerable, is what this compound adjective describes.

clue.text: Save time entering coastal area

indicators.note: 'time' enters, going inside the word for 'coastal area'

blocks.note: T is the standard abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Holidaymakers economising on travel time to the coast.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Save' could mean rescue, but the answer is the sense of keeping something back; T enters after the second letter.
explanation.definitionFit: To reserve or keep something back for later use is the verb phrase meaning to put by.
